resume.speaker: Alex
resume.text: I came to school worrying about our fair poster. Then an email threatened to close the account it's saved in.

story.speaker: Alex
story.text: Let's put their request next to the school contact details before I reply.

threats.situation: A second email claims to be the school's account helper. It mentions Alex's class and offers to remove the warning if Alex replies with a password. The sender says not to bother the teacher.
evidence: FROM: School Account Helper <helper@harbor-high-help.example>

Says: Keep this between us; your teacher is busy

choices.label: Reply with the password because the helper knows the class

events.text: Daniel receives a fraud call displaying his bank's identity.
The caller uses real business and account information to build credibility.
The caller discourages Daniel from contacting the bank independently.

reconstruction.finding: A real security event can be wrapped inside a false story. Verify the caller through an independently established channel.

opening.text: Daniel is closing his small business for the day. His phone rings. Unknown number.
Daniel ignores it. It rings again. Then again.

opening.speaker: Daniel
opening.text: Three times.

opening.speaker: Daniel
opening.text: If it's a customer, they'll leave a message.
A voicemail appears.

opening.speaker: Caller
opening.text: Mr. Santos, this is the Fraud Prevention Department regarding your business account. Immediate verification is required.

opening.speaker: Daniel
opening.text: ...Fraud prevention?
He calls Mia because his company has recently done business with BlueTech and he knows she has dealt with security incidents before.

opening.speaker: Daniel
opening.text: Mia, can I ask you something?

opening.speaker: Mia
opening.text: What happened?

opening.speaker: Daniel
opening.text: Does BlueTech ever contact suppliers about bank fraud?

opening.speaker: Mia
opening.text: Not like that.

opening.speaker: Daniel
opening.text: They know my business name.

opening.speaker: Mia
opening.text: Don't call them back yet.

opening.speaker: Daniel
opening.text: I'm not panicking.

opening.speaker: Mia
opening.text: I didn't say you were.

opening.speaker: Daniel
opening.text: I can hear you thinking it.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: Calling the bank myself was the only thing that actually answered anything.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: I kept asking them to prove themselves with information they already had.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: I was checking the real app and still letting the caller control the conversation.

ending.speaker: Security Assistant
ending.text: The first caller knew about the business.

ending.speaker: Mia
ending.text: The second knew how security verification works.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: And the third knew I had just called the real bank.

ending.speaker: Security Assistant
ending.text: Which means this isn't a random robocall.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: Good.

ending.speaker: Mia
ending.text: Good?

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: Now I know I'm not imagining it.

ending.speaker: Security Assistant
ending.text: Daniel.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: What?

ending.speaker: Security Assistant
ending.text: Do not turn this into a fight with whoever calls next.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: They called me.

ending.speaker: Security Assistant
ending.text: Exactly.

ending.speaker: Security Assistant
ending.text: They want you emotional.
Daniel pauses.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: ...Then next time I hang up.

ending.speaker: Mia
ending.text: Daniel.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: What?

ending.speaker: Mia
ending.text: That transaction they mentioned.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: The one from yesterday?

ending.speaker: Mia
ending.text: Who was it for?
Daniel checks.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: BlueTech.
Pause.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: Why?

ending.speaker: Security Assistant
ending.text: Probably nothing.

ending.speaker: Mia
ending.text: You don't sound like you believe that.

ending.speaker: Security Assistant
ending.text: I said probably.
Daniel's phone rings again. This time the caller ID says: PRIVATE NUMBER.
Daniel looks at Mia.

ending.speaker: Daniel
ending.text: I'm hanging up.
Before he can decline it, voicemail begins recording.

ending.speaker: Caller
ending.text: Mr. Santos, hanging up won't protect the account.
Daniel freezes.

ending.speaker: Caller
ending.text: We need you to stay on the line.

breach_contained.text: Breach contained. That call is cut off, but we still need to check what else it reached.

breach_contained.speaker: Daniel

threats.title: Fraud Department

story.text: Daniel receives another call. Caller ID displays the name of his real bank.

story.speaker: Caller
story.text: Mr. Santos, we detected an attempted ₱48,500 transfer from your business account. Before we freeze the account, I need to verify recent activity.

story.speaker: Daniel
story.text: How do you know my account number?

threats.situation: Daniel receives a call. Caller ID displays the name of his real bank. The caller says: "Mr. Santos, we detected an attempted ₱48,500 transfer from your business account. Before we freeze the account, I need to verify recent activity." The caller knows Daniel's full name, his business name, his bank name, an approximate account balance range, one recent legitimate transaction, and the last four digits of the business account. The caller does not immediately ask for a password.
evidence: Caller ID displays the name of Daniel's real bank
The caller accurately knows his business name and an approximate balance range
The caller correctly references one recent legitimate transaction
The caller has not asked for a password or OTP yet

choices.label: Continue the call because the caller has accurate private account information, while refusing to disclose passwords or OTPs.
choices.consequence: Withholding passwords feels safe, but staying on the call at all keeps Daniel exactly where the caller wants him — accurate account details were never the hard part to obtain.

choices.label: End the call and contact the bank using the number from Daniel's banking app/card/known official channel to verify whether a fraud case exists.
choices.consequence: Calling through the number on his own card confirms in minutes whether the bank's real fraud team actually flagged anything — and this caller never gets the chance to steer what happens next.

choices.label: Ask the caller to identify additional recent transactions before continuing.
choices.consequence: The caller lists another transaction correctly, but that only proves they already have access to Daniel's account activity — it doesn't prove they work for the bank.

choices.label: Keep the caller on the line while Daniel independently opens his real banking app and checks for the claimed transaction.
choices.consequence: The app does show a matching flagged attempt, but the caller is still on the line walking Daniel through what it means and what to do about it.

story_event.text: A new account-verification request appears while the call remains active.

story_event.speaker: Daniel
story_event.text: They're doing something while I'm talking to them.

threats.explanation: Vishing rarely opens by asking for a password — accurate account details build trust first. A caller having real information proves they can see the account somehow, not that they belong to the bank.

The caller instructs Daniel to keep the call active, open his banking app, not answer other calls, and wait for an account-security notification.

The caller frames staying on this call as protecting the account

timer.label: THE CALLER SAYS THE TRANSFER MAY PROCESS

timeout_story_event.title: CALL STATUS
timeout_story_event.text: The caller remains connected while Daniel hesitates.

choices.label: Stay on the call because the caller's warning about support-number impersonation is itself a legitimate security concern.
choices.consequence: The advice about impersonated support lines is real — the person giving it right now is using that true fact to keep Daniel from ever dialing a number they don't control.

story_event.title: ACCOUNT SECURITY REQUEST
story_event.text: A new request just appeared on the account while the call is still connected.

choices.label: End the call despite the warning and independently contact the bank using a previously trusted channel.
choices.consequence: Hanging up on the warning and calling the number Daniel already trusts reaches the bank's real fraud desk directly, with no chance for the caller to redirect that call somewhere else.

choices.label: Keep the caller connected but mute the call while Daniel checks the bank's official app and security notifications independently.
choices.consequence: The app check is genuinely independent, but the still-open call means the caller can hear Daniel come back and immediately reshape whatever he found.

choices.label: Ask the caller for a case number, then separately compare it against any case displayed in the real bank app before continuing.
choices.consequence: A case number appears in the app too, but that only confirms something is happening on the account — not that this caller is the one legitimately handling it.

threats.explanation: The attacker is using a true piece of security advice — support lines can be impersonated — to prevent the one action that would actually expose them: hanging up and dialing a number Daniel already trusts.

threats.title: Security Callback

story.speaker: Daniel
story.text: So now hanging up could be the dangerous thing?

story.speaker: Security Assistant
story.text: That's what they want you to believe.

story.speaker: Daniel
story.text: You keep saying 'they.'

story.speaker: Mia
story.text: Daniel—

story.speaker: Daniel
story.text: No.

story.speaker: Daniel
story.text: Someone knows my bank account. Someone knows my business. And now I'm supposed to just sit here while everybody tells me not to trust anyone?
Silence.

story.speaker: Daniel
story.text: ...Sorry.

story.speaker: Mia
story.text: You don't need to apologize.

story.speaker: Daniel
story.text: I don't like not knowing who's on the other side of the phone.

story.speaker: Security Assistant
story.text: That's exactly what they're exploiting.

Daniel independently contacts his bank. The legitimate bank confirms there was an attempted suspicious transfer, that it was blocked, and that they are reviewing the account. Daniel ends the legitimate call.
Minutes later, another call arrives. Caller ID again displays the bank's real support number.
